question.problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨1,2,k⟩$, $b=⟨-3,0,4⟩$, and $c=⟨2,-1,5⟩$ are coplanar.

$k=${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & k \\ -3 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}|+k\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(0\cdot 5-4\cdot (-1))-2((-3)\cdot 5-4\cdot 2)+k((-3)\cdot (-1)-0\cdot 2) \\  & =4-2(-15-8)+3k \\  & =50+3k\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 50+3k & =0 \\ k & =-\frac{50}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=-\frac{50}{3}.$
